record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: For each conformal field theory in the ADE family that arises as the scaling limit of an integrable lattice model, find a corresponding model that can actually be constructed by constructive methods.

evidence.quote: there exist integrable lattice models of the ADE type which scale to conformal field theories of the [BPZ] classification at their critical point [Pa]; can we find a model which can be built with constructive methods for every such conformal theory?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. The BPZ classification of two-dimensional conformal field theories with central charge c<1 (the minimal models) is organized by pairs of simply-laced Dynkin diagrams, giving the so-called ADE family of rational conformal field theories. It is known that for each diagram in the ADE family there exists an integrable lattice statistical-mechanics model (of solid-on-solid / RSOS / Pasquier type, whose configuration space carries a representation of the Temperley–Lieb algebra associated with the diagram) whose scaling limit at criticality is conjecturally the corresponding ADE conformal field theory.

Problem. For each conformal field theory in the ADE family (equivalently, for each simply-laced Dynkin diagram), exhibit a two-dimensional lattice model whose scaling limit at criticality is that conformal field theory and which can be rigorously constructed using the methods of constructive (Euclidean) quantum field theory — that is, for which one can rigorously define the model on the lattice, prove existence of the continuum (scaling) limit of its correlation functions, and verify that the limiting theory satisfies the axioms (e.g. Osterwalder–Schrader / Wightman) of a conformal field theory matching the prescribed ADE minimal model.
artifact.status_search_result: Web sources indicate that rigorous constructive/scaling-limit results connecting lattice models to their conjectured CFTs exist only in a few cases (notably the Gaussian free field and the Ising model, where discrete complex analysis yields Virasoro structure). A complete constructive realization of every ADE minimal model as the scaling limit of an integrable lattice model has not been achieved; extending these techniques to general rational CFTs (anyonic chains, c<1 minimal models beyond Ising) is explicitly stated as an open direction in recent literature.

status_evidence.title: Conformal Field Theory at the Lattice Level: Discrete Complex Analysis and Virasoro Structure
status_evidence.snippet: A positive answer has been given for the discrete Gaussian free field and for the Ising model, by connecting discrete complex analysis with Virasoro symmetry expected in their scaling limits.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous lattice-to-CFT constructions exist only for special cases (GFF, Ising), not for the full ADE family.

status_evidence.title: Conformal Field Theory from Lattice Fermions
status_evidence.snippet: To handle arbitrary rational CFTs, it will be necessary to address lattice models involving anyonic chains... To allow for a central charge c<1, a natural extension is needed.
status_evidence.claim: Treating general c<1 (ADE minimal) CFTs constructively from lattice models remains an open extension.

status_evidence.title: A-D-E Classification of Conformal Field Theories - Scholarpedia
status_evidence.snippet: The c<1 minimal models admit a realization as integrable statistical systems on a lattice... leading to graphs of ADE type.
status_evidence.claim: ADE minimal models are conjecturally realized as scaling limits of integrable lattice models.
